summary: The milestone-scoped timing detector attributed 0 experiment commits since activation, so total_wall_time_minutes=0, experiments_completed=0 and compute_bound_experiments_count=0 — this is the recurring false-zero detector gap (documented .363-.403, now extending to .404), NOT an idle milestone. With 0 compute-bound tasks attributed, both RTX 3090s sitting idle at the snapshot is correct behaviour, so gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is null and the idle GPU is not a bottleneck.
bottlenecks_identified: Observability, not execution: the milestone-scoped timing detector false-zeroed again (experiments_completed=0) even though the milestone executed end-to-end on disk — the same gap recorded every milestone since .363. Retro timing numbers are therefore uninformative about real wall-time and cannot rank any experiment.

No write-time timing stamps: because the detector attributes 0 experiments, there is no per-experiment duration_s/compute_bound signal to populate slowest_experiments, so bottleneck ranking has nothing to act on this milestone.

GPU idle is explicitly NOT flagged: with 0 compute-bound tasks attributed (gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks=null), the 0% utilization on both RTX 3090s at the snapshot is correct behaviour, not a bottleneck.
improvements_suggested: Repair the milestone-scoped timing detector: add an mtime scan of results/experiment_*.json within the activation->capstone window plus a changelog-window fallback, so experiments executed since activation are attributed instead of reporting 0.
Stamp duration_s + compute_bound + inference_substrate at artifact write-time (in scripts/experiment_template.py) so retros can rank slowest experiments without depending on git-commit attribution.
Auto-emit detector_gap_suspected=true when on-disk artifacts exist for the active milestone window but the detector attributes 0, converting a silently-recurring gap into a self-flagging one.

Keep the established workaround: when the detector returns 0, the retro reads the on-disk capstone (this milestone: exp4379) for the narrative — but this manual re-discovery is the cost the detector fix would remove.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix the milestone-scoped timing detector (mtime scan within the activation->capstone window + changelog-window fallback) — this single fix ends the 40+-milestone false-zero streak and restores all downstream retro timing signal.
Add write-time duration_s/compute_bound/inference_substrate stamping in scripts/experiment_template.py so slowest-experiment ranking is detector-independent.
Auto-emit detector_gap_suspected when artifacts exist on disk but the detector reports 0, so the false-zero self-flags instead of being re-discovered each milestone.
meta_reflection: The recurring lesson holds at .404: the operational failure is observability, not execution — the milestone ran cleanly end-to-end (clean, unflagged capstone exp4379; no doomed reruns; no flagged artifacts) yet the timing detector reported 0 for the 40-plus-th consecutive milestone, forcing the retro to reconstruct ground truth from on-disk artifact mtimes. Until the detector is repaired (mtime + changelog fallback) and duration_s is stamped at write-time, every retro keeps paying this manual re-discovery cost while the underlying research loop is healthy; the realistic wall-time speedup from these tooling changes is small (execution is already efficient) — the payoff is observability and analyst time, not faster experiments.
